note: Every look sentence and round line on record, 122: the 98 the 13 Oct 2026 forensics bench wrote on the repo's own Abyss 13 to 11 (valorant-match-abyss-13-11.json), verbatim, and the 24 of the player's library (the 12 sentences of its looks and the 12 round lines of the rounds looked at), retyped as equivalents: the same first word, capitalised words, digits and listed phrases, the other words changed. test:forensics holds the server's name gate to them: none names a player.

sentences.text: You died at A Site, alone in the open with no teammate close enough to trade, and the Viper's Marshal finished you while your team was spread out and committed to B.
Hold A Vent tight with your Bandit and do not push out alone, so a teammate is close enough to trade the Viper if she takes you down.
You pushed onto A Site alone while your teammates were committed elsewhere, and the Viper's Marshal caught you with no one close enough to trade the kill.
Hold A Vent with your Bandit and stay tight with the team instead of pushing out alone, since the team was committed to B.
You were standing at A Vent, peeking out with an Operator and no smoke or flash in place, and the enemy you died to was still unseen in this frame.
Hold the corner and wait for a teammate's smoke or flash, or ping the enemy's position so your team can trade before you step out.
You pushed onto A Site at 1:20 with no teammate near you, and an enemy Viper killed you with a Marshal from the open ground in front of the site entrance while the rest of your team held elsewhere.
Stay with your Bandit at A Vent until your team is ready to take A Site together, so a single Marshal shot cannot catch you alone.
You peeked wide into the open at A Vent with no utility or information first, and the killer was waiting for you as you came out.

Getting the first kill at B Link is good, but dying ten seconds later points to an overextension without dash ready. Use your mobility to reposition safely once you have information rather than staying in a vulnerable spot.

Hugging a wall slows your acceleration and makes you an easy target for sharpshooters. You should step out of cover and peek angles with movement instead of staying static.
Rotating into a site without information hands the enemy your positional advantage. Stick to the site that has already worked for the opponent to gather intel.
